title: Fauna Unified Test State
description:
Canonical app state format for E2E test state injection and inspection across all 7 apps.

NULL CONVENTION: Each section under 'data' MUST be null if the client has not implemented serialization for that section. An empty array [] means 'implemented but no data'. This distinction lets the test framework skip unimplemented sections (null) vs fail on missing data ([]).

COMPOSE (write-only): set_state({"compose": {"file": "/path"}}) tells the test agent to attach a file via upload_blob(), bypassing native file pickers. Web overrides this with Playwright's set_input_files(). All native clients must implement this handler.

session.description: Authentication and identity state. Write: inject credentials to log in. Read: verify auth status.

nav.description: Navigation state. Write: set_state({nav: {stack: [{view: 'feed'}]}}) to navigate. Read: verify current page.

settings.description: User settings. Read: verify current inbox mode, spam threshold, etc.

messages.description: Transient UI messages. Write: inject error/warning/info for testing. Read: verify displayed messages. Messages clear on navigation.

compose.description:
WRITE-ONLY. Injected during set_state to trigger test agent actions. Not returned by get_state.

Full compose.file flow: set_state({compose: {file: '/path'}}) → test agent calls upload_blob(path) → receives blob hash → stores hash in compose context → next post submission includes the hash as an attachment. Web clients use Playwright set_input_files() instead.

compose.post: creates a post programmatically, bypassing compose UI. Essential for platforms where compose-text-field is inaccessible (macOS detail pane). The test agent calls the feed post creation API directly.

file.description: Absolute path to a file. The test agent calls upload_blob() and attaches the result to the current compose context. Web clients use Playwright set_input_files() instead.

post.description: Create a post programmatically without UI interaction. The test agent calls the feed API directly. Use this on platforms where compose-text-field is inaccessible (macOS). Web clients may also use this to avoid WASM timing issues in honesty checks.

tags.description: Tag strings WITHOUT # prefix. The UI adds # for display; state and API store raw strings.

data.description: App data sections. Each section is null if not implemented by the client, or contains real data if implemented. NEVER use empty arrays/objects for unimplemented sections — use null.

timestamp.description: Milliseconds since epoch. Mapped from API field 'created_at'. The state protocol field is 'timestamp' (not 'created_at') for all data sections.

tags.description: Tag strings WITHOUT # prefix (e.g. 'rust', not '#rust'). The UI displays tags with # prefix. The action layer normalizes to #-prefixed when returning tags to tests. State and API always store raw strings.

verification.description: Whether THIS client cryptographically verified the post's signed envelope (security.md § App display of unverified content; mapped from PostSummary.verification). 'Failed' drives the unverified-source-badge; 'Unchecked' (default — a trusted nest-index list card with no envelope) and 'Verified' render none. Optional: clients that haven't serialized it omit it.

authoring_origin.description: Whether an EXTERNAL APP authored this post as the account, via a delegated authoring sub-key (atproto-pds-full.md § D10 → Audit; mapped from PostSummary.authoring_origin). 'Delegated' drives the delegated-origin-badge; 'Direct' (the account signed it itself) and 'Unknown' render none. 'Unknown' is BOTH the undecoded nest-index card AND the verification-failed case, deliberately — an unverified wire's cert is exactly what nothing authenticated, so its origin claim is never rendered. Orthogonal to 'verification': the two answer independent questions. Optional: clients that haven't serialized it omit it.
